# Q&A Log — Cross-Cutting: Roles & Departments
# Append-only. Do not edit past entries; add new dated entries instead.

## 2026-09-22 — Q1: Should Roles & Departments become a new cross-cutting pillar?

**Context:** User paused before starting Workflow/Process (domain 7) to
vet a structural gap: roles had been accumulating as provisional
plain-text labels in every completed domain's Access Rules column, each
flagged "pending Interface/Human domain" (domain 9 — last in row-major
order). Workflow/Process is exactly where role-to-workflow mapping
starts to matter, resurfacing the original chicken-and-egg problem from
the framework's very first design conversation.

**Bucket:** [Org-decision]/Human-only — structural framework decision.

**Options presented:** (a) cross-cutting pillar now, alongside Governance
and Security [Recommended]; (b) pull all of Domain 9 forward out of
row-major order; (c) keep deferring until literal Domain 9.

**Answer:** (a) Cross-cutting pillar now.

## 2026-09-22 — Q2: Should Data Owner/Steward/Custodian/Governance Council move here?

**Bucket:** [Org-decision]/Human-only.

**Options presented:** (a) stay owned by Data/Metadata, referenced here
[Recommended]; (b) move into this cross-cutting registry.

**Answer:** (a) Stay owned by Data/Metadata. This registry's Definitions
file includes a "Referenced Terms (owned elsewhere)" section pointing to
all four.

## 2026-09-22 — Q3: How should Departments align to the 7 layers?

**Bucket:** [Org-decision]/Human-only.

**Options presented:** (a) one department per domain, clean 1:1
[Recommended]; (b) allow a department to span multiple domains; (c)
free-form, framework asserts no alignment at all.

**Answer:** (b) Allow a department to span multiple domains. Realized as
Platform Engineering spanning Infrastructure + Networking, and Security &
Compliance spanning all 7 layers as a cross-cutting reviewer rather than
an owner of any one domain. Recorded in 02-taxonomies.md's Department ↔
Domain Alignment table, explicitly flagged as illustrative/generalized,
not prescriptive for any specific adopting organization.

**Bucket:** [Org-decision]/Human-only.

**Options presented:** (a) retrofit now, before Workflow/Process

**Answer:** (a) Retrofit now. Applied to: 01-infrastructure/07-access-
rules.md, 02-networking/07-access-rules.md,
03-system-architecture/07-access-rules.md,
05-data-metadata/07-access-rules.md, and cross-cutting/access-rules.md
(CCAR-1/2/3) — see each file's own _qa log for its retrofit entry.

---

**Design note on scope:** this registry deliberately stays smaller than a
full domain (23 owned terms vs. 58-66 for a domain's Definitions) — it
covers the *generic* role/department vocabulary that recurs across
domains, not an exhaustive HR taxonomy. Domain-specific governance roles
stay owned by their owning domain (Q2's resolution) rather than being
absorbed here, keeping this registry genuinely cross-cutting rather than
a second home for domain-specific content.

**Still unresolved (carried forward from Q3, not decided here):** DevOps/

## 2026-09-22 — Q7: Data Platform ownership — Application Engineering co-ownership challenged

**Context:** Immediate follow-up to Q6's Data Platform insertion. When the
Databases & Storage cluster moved from System Architecture to the new
Data Platform domain, ownership was provisionally modeled as Application
Engineering + Data Governance & Engineering co-owning it — reasoning
purely inherited from where the terms used to live (System Architecture),
not a considered decision. User pushed back: application teams consume
a database, they don't design or operate the platform it runs on — that's
data engineering/data architecture's job, the same way Platform
Engineering (not Application Engineering) owns Infrastructure even though
every application depends on it.

**Bucket:** [Org-decision]/Human-only.

**Options presented:** (a) Data Governance & Engineering owns Data
Platform outright, Application Engineering just consumes it; (b) a new
dedicated department owns it alone; (c) split more precisely along the
multi-department model, no ownership claim from Application Engineering
at all.

**Answer:** (a), refined — Data Governance & Engineering owns Domain 4
(Data Platform) and Domain 5 (Data/Metadata) outright, matching the
Platform Engineering precedent (one department spanning multiple
domains). Within that department, ownership of Data Platform specifically
is split across two distinct, newly-defined Positional Roles rather than
held generically by the department: **Data Architect**
(ccrole-data-architect, design — data models, storage/streaming
technology selection) and **Data Engineer** (ccrole-data-engineer,
build/operate — pipelines, ETL/ELT, schema migrations, day-to-day
operation), which co-own Domain 4 jointly. User was explicit these are
two separate roles, not one combined "Data Architect/Engineer" role.

**Applied to:** cross-cutting/roles-and-departments/01-definitions.md
(Application Engineering and Data Governance & Engineering department
entries rewritten; Data Architect and Data Engineer added under Generic
Positional Roles), 02-taxonomies.md (tree + Department ↔ Domain Alignment
table), 03-ontologies.md (two new Positional Role → Department Membership
edges, plus a `constrains` edge capturing the design-precedes-build
relationship between the two new roles), org-chart.md (same).

**Still open:** whether Data Architect/Data Engineer should also have a
stake in any other domain (e.g., Data/Metadata's Logical/Physical Data
Model terms overlap conceptually with Data Architect's design scope, but
Data/Metadata's existing Data Owner/Steward/Custodian roles were not
touched here) — not raised, not decided, flagged for a future pass if it
turns out to matter in practice.

## 2026-09-22 — Q8: Business Intelligence / Reporting domain, Analytics Engineer role, BI department

**Context:** Immediate follow-up to Q7. User identified that Data
Platform's Semantic Layer and Data/Metadata's Metric definitions don't
guarantee what actually ends up in a report — Business Analysts and BI
Analysts build self-service report-level models (calculated fields,
extracts, blended sources) directly inside the reporting tool, which can
silently diverge from the official definitions. Discussion converged on:
(1) this needs its own domain, not just a role, since it's a real
technical artifact layer (report-level data models) the existing domains
don't model; (2) documentation must include source-to-target mapping,
extending Data/Metadata's existing lineage concepts one hop further; (3)
much of that mapping should be tool-derived (OpenMetadata/DataHub-style
catalog platforms auto-extract BI-tool lineage) rather than hand-written,
with the framework requiring registration + certification status rather
than a bespoke manual doc process; (4) a distinct "Analytics Engineer"
role exists between Data Engineer and BI, building the transformation/
semantic layer.

**Bucket:** [Org-decision]/Human-only (domain insertion, role/department
structure) + [Standard]/AI-draftable (the mechanical renumbering).

**Answer:**
- New domain: **Business Intelligence / Reporting**, inserted as domain
  6 (Workflow/Process 6→7, Harness 7→8, Interface/Human 8→9). See
  00-framework/domain-axis-definition.md and
  00-framework/ea-framework-alignment.md.
- New term `data-metric` (Data/Metadata) — the official metric
  definition — and `dp-semantic-layer` (Data Platform) — where a Metric
  gets materialized for querying — added to bridge Data Platform/Data-
  Metadata into the new domain's eventual Definitions.
- New role **Analytics Engineer** (`ccrole-analytics-engineer`), third
  co-owner of Data Platform (domain 4) alongside Data Architect/Data
  Engineer, home department Data Governance & Engineering — builds the
  Semantic Layer.
- New department **Business Intelligence & Analytics**
  (`ccdept-business-intelligence-analytics`), owns domain 6 outright.
  Two new roles under it, kept separate per explicit instruction (not
  merged into one role): **Business Analyst / Report Builder**
  (`ccrole-business-analyst-report-builder`, the self-service builder —
  the role most likely to create an undocumented/diverging model) and
  **BI Analyst/Developer** (`ccrole-bi-analyst-developer`, builds more
  formal distributed reports, typically reviews/promotes a Business
  Analyst's model to Certified).

**Applied to:** 00-framework/domain-axis-definition.md,
00-framework/ea-framework-alignment.md,
00-framework/term-linking-convention.md (new `bi` prefix),
00-framework/setup.sh, directory renumbering (07-workflow-process,
08-harness, 09-interface-human), new 06-bi-reporting/ scaffold,
05-data-metadata/01-definitions.md + 02-taxonomies.md + 03-ontologies.md
(Metric term + relationships), 04-data-platform/01-definitions.md +
02-taxonomies.md + 03-ontologies.md (Semantic Layer term + relationships),
this registry's 01-definitions.md, 02-taxonomies.md, 03-ontologies.md,
org-chart.md.

**Still not done:** Business Intelligence / Reporting domain's own
Definitions/Taxonomies/Ontologies (Report, Dashboard, Report Data Model,
Calculated Field, Data Extract, Certified Dataset/Report, Row-Level
Security, and a `bi-source-to-target-mapping` term extending
`data-lineage`) — scaffolded as not-started, to be drafted next. Its
Policies column will carry the certification-gate rule discussed
(cannot reach Certified/broad-distribution status without registration +
source-to-target mapping in the metadata registry); its Tooling column
will extend Data/Metadata's OpenMetadata entry rather than naming a
second platform.
